prompts.dolphin:
Use case: precise-object-edit, identity-preserve. Create a TRANSPARENT separated-parts atlas for a rear-view static paper-doll of the EXISTING pet. The input sheet has side views LEFT and REAR views RIGHT, three growth rows. Use ONLY the RIGHT COLUMN rear designs as canonical. Preserve exact colors, gradients, proportions, silhouette details and finely painted glossy illustration style. This is decomposition into parts, NOT a redesign, not a mirror of the front.
Wide high-resolution atlas with THREE evenly spaced rows, representing stages1,2,3. Exactly SIX columns. Same camera looking STRAIGHT at the BACK for every piece. No eyes, face, smile or belly painted on the back. No front or side view. Each isolated part includes a small hidden overlap root so it can be layered onto main body without a gap. No mechanical joints, no text/labels/grid/background/shadows. Real transparent alpha and transparent gutters, at least 20px between any parts. Nothing touches or crops at canvas edge. Within each row keep consistent relative scale rather than enlarging tiny pieces arbitrarily.Columns: 1 smooth blue rear HEAD+TORSO, WITHOUT either pectoral flipper, dorsal fin, tail stem or tail fluke; fill the areas behind removed appendages with matching blue painted skin. 2 anatomical LEFT pectoral flipper seen from rear (viewer-left), complete root. 3 anatomical RIGHT pectoral flipper seen from rear (viewer-right), complete root. 4 the narrow midline DORSAL FIN seen EDGE-ON from behind, shaped exactly like the upright tapered center fin in the rear reference, not the broad side-profile crest. 5 short tapered TAIL STEM ONLY, blue, with overlapping roots at both ends. 6 the complete TWO-LOBED TAIL FLUKE joined in the middle, seen from behind, both symmetric lobes as ONE part, its little stem root at the TOP middle. No disconnected flukes.
Stage1 plump round rear body, tiny fins and little two-lobed tail. Stage2 elongated body and longer fins. Stage3 exact original flowing pectoral fins and broad two-lobed fluke with cream/aqua tips. Keep gradients and contour colors and growth differences. All three forms point away from viewer with head up and tail down.
